audience.risks:
A sticky role is a dead end waiting to happen. Dan opens the assessor door once on his own laptop and then cannot find the questionnaire. Three guards, all cheap: .brand always returns to Start, Start always carries both doors, and Settings shows the current role with a one-click switch. A first run has no stored role and no chosen door, so the very first visit shows Start with both doors and no path in the header at all, which means his first demo shows him everything.

Hiding a destination reads as a regression in a government demo. Someone will ask where the review tab went. The answer has to be one sentence he can repeat: the assessor view is at the same address with #review on the end. Put that sentence in Settings beside the role switch.

The repaint model kills the animation she asked for, and this is the one part of the plan that is not free. paint() clears #app and rebuilds all 4,049 nodes on every score click. A rebuilt element has no previous width, so transition: width .2s ease on .step-bar i never plays, and 176 score clicks produce 176 silent jumps. Any sparkly completion effect dies the same way. The chrome has to be built once and updated in place, which is the pattern this codebase already uses three times inside questionBlock (paintScores, paintChosen, paintOther) and once in evidenceEditor. Narrowing the repaint is real work and should be costed with the progress bar, not with the role split. Say that to her before she expects the sparkle in the same sitting.

The rubric is data and the strip has to survive it. Four domains fit one row at 940px. Seven do not, under the present wrapping grid. The horizontal scroll rule handles it, and it should be tested against a rubric with more domains before she demos, because "any of those counts can change" is written into the constraints.

Accessibility debt travels with the move and gets louder. The relocated strip is still a nav with no accessible name, .step.on still has no aria-current, and .step-bar still has no progressbar role. Pinning it makes it the most-read element on the page for a screen-reader user, so add aria-label on the nav, aria-current="page" on the current step, and either a progressbar role with values or plain text that states the count. Related and still owed: the Business page has one h2 across 6 sections and 61 questions. Making the strip permanent does not fix that.

The genuine risk of doing nothing about roles: none in the next month. Three people, no network, no shared storage. This is a change worth making because it pays for the sticky tabs, and for no other reason. If it starts growing (an accounts idea, a second file, a build flag), stop and keep the tab.

survey:
Verified against the on-disk source. Note: `src/main.ts` and `src/styles.css` were rewritten at 16:24:41, after my first read of them, so the shell facts below come from a re-read; `views-submit.ts`, `views-review.ts` and the rubric are unchanged. All measurements are from `dist/index.html` rebuilt at 16:25 from that source, driven in a real browser at 1440x900 (content column 940px), on the Business Architecture page with a lifecycle stage picked.

# BASELINE SURVEY — current questionnaire rendering

## 1. How the submit view is assembled

`main.ts paint()` rebuilds `#app` from scratch on every paint:

```
#app
  div.chrome                      [STICKY top:0, z-index 30]
    header.topbar                 brand + nav.path (Start › Fill it in › Review submissions) + .icon-btn gear
    div.marking-banner            only in submit/results
  main.body                       max-width 940px, margin 1.15rem auto 6rem
    ...renderSubmit() output...
  div.marking-banner.print-only   display:none on screen
  footer.sitefoot
```

`views-submit.ts renderSubmit()` appends, in order, into `main.body`:

1. `nav.stepper` — `stepper()`
2. either `aboutSection()` (+ an optional `section.card.warn` if no lifecycle stage) **or** one `section.card` domain header plus one `section.card.section` per section — `sectionBlock()` in a loop
3. `section.card.actions` — `pager()`, the Back / Next buttons
4. `div.sticky-footer` — `footerBar()`

Page state is a module-level `let page: 'about' | string` in `views-submit.ts`. It is not persisted, so reopening the tool always lands on Overview even when the draft is half-answered.

## 2. Visual separation at each level, as built today

**Domain page (`renderSubmit`).** One `section.card` holds `h2` = domain label with a `span.pill` score inside the heading, the domain description as `p.muted`, and `p.muted.small` reading `"25% of the overall score. 12 of 61 answered."` Measured 115px tall. It is the only thing on the page that names the domain, and it is in normal flow at the top.

**Section (`sectionBlock`).** `section.card.section > details > summary.section-summary` + an unclassed `div` holding the questions. Separation is real but thin: `.card` gives a 1px `--line` border, 10px radius, `--shadow`, and 0.85rem bottom margin — but `.card.section` overrides padding down to `.35rem .75rem` (a normal card is `1.05rem 1.15rem`). The summary row is a flex line of: `span.pill.small` score, `span.section-title` (a **span**, not a heading), `span.muted.small` = `"5% of this domain"`, `span.muted.small` = `"14/14"`, and an optional `span.badge`. Disclosure triangle is a CSS border triangle on `.section-summary::before`, rotated 90° by `details[open] > .section-summary::before`. Measured: summary row 43px; section 1 (14 questions) 4,415px open, 56px closed.

**Question (`questionBlock`).** `div.question` and nothing more — `border-top: 1px solid var(--line)`, `padding: .85rem 0 .5rem`, killed on `.question:first-of-type`. No background, no card, no left rail, no id, no `data-qid`. The dividing hairline is the same colour and weight as the section card's own border. **This is the literal mechanism behind "it all blends into one vertical sheet": inside a section, 14 to 61 questions are separated only by a 1px `--line` rule on a flat white ground.** Measured 300–323px per unanswered question.

**Question internals**, in DOM order:
- `div.q-head` — `span.qid` (mono chip, e.g. `BU-Q1`), `span.q-text` (font-weight 550, `flex: 1 1 20rem`), optional `span.badge`
- optional `p.muted.small` help text (never fires — see §9)
- `details.ladder-box` — collapsed, summary "What the numbers mean" in accent blue, containing `ul.ladder` of all 11 rungs as `li` with `b` value + `i` name + label
- `div.score-row` — 11 `button.score-btn.v0…v10`, each `2.05rem` wide, plus `label.na` with a checkbox
- `div.chosen.muted.small` — the selected rung's name and full sentence, empty until scored
- optional picklist `div.field` (never fires — see §9)
- `label.field` "Why that score, in your words" + `textarea rows=2`
- `div.evidence` from `evidenceEditor()`

**Score row.** Selected state is `button.score-btn.on.v7` → white text on `--s7`, `border-color: transparent`, `--shadow`. Unselected is `--surface` with `--line-2` border and `--ink-2` text. The 11 `--s0…--s10` colours are Dan's ramp. No `aria-pressed`, no radiogroup, no group label: the chosen score is signalled by colour and weight only.

**Justification.** A plain `label.field` with a 2-row textarea. `oninput` writes `ans.justification` and calls `autosave(a)` only — no repaint, so typing is smooth and focus is safe.

**Evidence (`evidenceEditor`).** `div.evidence` is the one tinted block inside a question: `--surface-2` background, 1px `--line`, `--radius-sm`, 0.55/0.65rem padding. Contains `div.ev-head` (bold "Evidence" + a muted prompt), then one `div.ev-item` per reference separated by `1px dashed --line-2`, then a `div.actions` with the "Add evidence" button. Each item is `div.ev-row` (a 4-column grid: title / kind select / classification select / Remove) over `div.ev-row2` (attach control + location or note). Unmarked evidence gets `.ev-item.unmarked` — `--bad-bg` plus a 1px red ring — and `select.needs-marking`. An attachment renders as `div.att`, a green-tinted inline chip with the filename, size, Open and Detach.

## 3. The domain stepper, exactly as it works now

`stepper()` returns `nav.stepper` containing five `button.step`: Overview plus one per domain. Each holds `span.step-label`, `span.step-count` (`"12 of 61"`, mono), and `span.step-bar > i` with an inline `style="width:NN%"`. Class flags: `.on` for the current page (accent border + 1px accent ring), `.complete` when `done === total` (green-ish border, green bar fill). Labels are shortened by `shortLabel()`, which strips `/\s*&\s*\w+/` then a trailing `Architecture`, giving Business / Data / Application / Technology.

Layout: `display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(150px, 1fr))`, so at 940px all five sit on one 70px row. Clicking sets `page`, repaints, and calls `window.scrollTo({top: 0})`.

**It is in normal document flow.** Measured: stepper occupies document y = 104 to 174. It is gone after ~174px of scroll — under 1% of a 20,190px page. The domain header card is gone by ~300px. From then on nothing on screen names the domain or the section. This is complaint 3, and the measured cause is that `.stepper` has no `position` rule at all.

`pager()` puts Back / Next in a card **after** all 61 questions, roughly 20,000px down. The sticky footer offers "Save to a file" and "See my results" but no way forward to the next domain.

## 4. Section collapsing, exactly as it works now

One line does all of it: `el('details', { open: ss.answered < ss.total }, …)`.

The `el()` helper skips `false` attributes and sets `open=""` for `true`, so a section is open while incomplete and closed when complete. Two consequences, both reproduced in the browser:

- **A section collapses under the cursor the instant its last question is scored.** Section 1 went from 4,415px to 56px on that click; the page shrank from 20,190px to 15,831px while the user's viewport stayed at the same scroll offset.
- **Open state is derived, never stored.** Manually reopening a completed section, then scoring any question anywhere on the page, force-closes it again. Verified: `reopenedSurvivedRepaint: false`.

A fresh assessment therefore renders every section open: Business is 6 sections, 61 questions, 20,190px, 22.4 viewport-heights at 900px.

Edge case: a section whose questions are all marked n/a has `total === 0`, so `0 < 0` is false and it renders closed.

## 5. Sticky versus scrolls away

| Element | Behaviour | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| `div.chrome` (topbar + marking banner) | `position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 30` | 86px total (topbar 59 + banner 27), pinned at scrollY 6000 |
| `nav.stepper` | static, scrolls away | 70px, gone by y≈174 |
| domain header `.card` | static, scrolls away | 115px, gone by y≈300 |
| `summary.section-summary` | static, scrolls away with its card | 43px; at scrollY 6000 **all six were off screen** while inside "Demonstrated Engagement" |
| `div.sticky-footer` | `position: sticky; bottom: .6rem; z-index: 25` | 90px, pinned 9.6px above the viewport bottom |
| `th` in results/review tables | `position: sticky; top: 0` | not on the questionnaire |

Net usable band between the two pinned blocks at 900px: 900 − 86 − 100 ≈ **714px, about 2.2 questions**. Measured mid-scroll, exactly **one** question sat fully inside it.

`sticky-footer` content: an optional `div.gate.small` strip (first blocking marking problem, amber), then `div.footer-inner` with `div.footer-score` (`span.pill` overall score + maturity label + `"12 of 176 answered"`) and `div.footer-actions` (Save to a file, See my results). **The only always-visible progress indicator today is that muted "N of M answered" sentence.** There is no bar, no percentage, no per-section or per-domain progress once the stepper scrolls off.

## 6. The repaint model — the hardest constraint on any proposal

Every score click and every n/a toggle calls `changed()`, which is `repaint` from `renderSubmit`, which is `repaintApp()`, which `setRepaint` bound to `main.ts paint()`. That clears `#app` and rebuilds the whole tree. Verified by node identity: after one score click, both the clicked `.question` node and the `.topbar` node were different objects.

So on each score click the app throws away and rebuilds 4,049 DOM nodes, including 67 `<details>`. Scroll offset happened to survive (the document height barely moves), but any focus is destroyed and any element-level state that is not derived from the model is lost. A proposal that wants a per-question completion animation, a sticky section header driven by `IntersectionObserver`, or user-controlled collapse must either survive that teardown or narrow the repaint. Localized repaints already exist as a pattern inside `questionBlock` (`paintScores`, `paintChosen`, `paintOther`) and `evidenceEditor` (`paint`), and the justification textarea deliberately does not repaint at all — the comment in `aboutSection` explains why.

## 7. Print baseline

`@media print` currently:
```css
.topbar, .sticky-footer, .actions, .sitefoot, .stepper, button, .filelabel { display: none !important; }
details { display: block; } details > summary { display: none; }
```
Three consequences for a printed questionnaire, all present today:
- **The score selector disappears.** Scores are `button.score-btn`, so the answer itself does not print. Only the `div.chosen` sentence survives.
- **Section titles disappear.** The title, weight and section score live inside `summary`, which is hidden.
- All 61 ladder `details` expand, printing 11 rungs per question.
- `.marking-banner.print-only { display: none }` is never overridden inside `@media print`, so the intended foot-of-page marking (see the comment in `paint()`) does not actually print. The sticky top banner does print, restyled to black on white with a 2px bottom rule.

`.card { page-break-inside: avoid }` is set, which will fight any 4,400px section card.

## 8. Accessibility baseline

- **One `<h2>` on the entire Business page** ("Business Architecture"). Section titles are spans in a summary; question text is `span.q-text`. There is no heading outline over 6 sections and 61 questions, and no `fieldset`/`role="group"`/`aria-labelledby` tying a score row to its question.
- 930 focusable elements inside `main.body`; 15 per question (11 score buttons, n/a checkbox, ladder summary, textarea, Add evidence).
- `.step.on` and `.score-btn.on` carry no `aria-current` / `aria-pressed`; `nav.stepper` has no accessible name.
- `.step-bar` has no `role="progressbar"` or value; the text alternative is `.step-count`.
- The `h2` on the domain card contains the score pill, so it reads as "Business Architecture 5.2".
- Focus is handled well: one shared `:focus-visible` rule gives every button, input, select, textarea, summary and file label a 2px accent outline with 2px offset.
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is already respected, but only for the one animation that exists.

## 9. Facts about the data that constrain proposals

- 4 domains at 25% each; 20 sections; 176 questions. Business 61 in 6, Data 39 in 5, Application 37 in 4, Technology 39 in 5. Largest section is Data Architecture & Standards at 12; smallest is Accessibility, Interoperability & Usability at 3.
- Business section weights sum to 80%, not 100%. It is surfaced as `rubric.importWarnings` in Settings and the roll-up normalises.
- Every question in `rubric.v1-dan.json` carries exactly four fields: `id`, `sheetRef`, `text`, `weight` (all weight 1). **No question has `help`, `picklist`, `anchors`, `evidencePrompt`, `nextSteps` or `stageExpectation`.** So `questionBlock`'s help paragraph, picklist block and per-question badge, and the results page's next-steps list, are live code with no data behind them today. A proposal may assume they are absent but must not delete them.
- Question text runs 67 to 141 characters, median 116 — reliably two lines at 940px, never one.
- `stageExpectation` exists only on the four "Defining the Current State" sections, and only for `discovery` and `alpha` (`low-ok`, multiplier 0.25). At the other five lifecycle stages **no `.badge` ever renders anywhere in the questionnaire.**
- The 11 anchors have `value`, `colour`, `name` (Absent, Critical Gaps, Fragmented … Symbiotic) and a full sentence `label`.
- Maturity bands: Critical Risk 0, Developing 3, Baseline Ready 5, Advanced 7, Leading Practice 9.

## 10. Already present and reusable

- **Progress bar primitive**: `.step-bar` / `.step-bar i` with `transition: width .2s ease` and a green `.step.complete` variant. Also `.bar-track` / `.bar-fill` with the `b0…b10` ramp and `transition: width .25s ease` on the results page.
- **`tone(v)` and `bar(v)`** in `dom.ts`, mapping a score to `t0…t10` / `b0…b10`; the 11 `--s0…--s10` tokens exist in both light and dark.
- **`.pill` / `.pill.small`** — the score chip already used on domain, section and audit rows.
- **`.badge` / `.badge-warn` / `.badge-soft`** — small pill labels, currently unused with this rubric.
- **`.kpi-row` / `.kpi` / `.kpi-num` / `.kpi-label`** — a ready counter strip, used only on the reviewer side, directly usable for an always-visible progress readout.
- **`.section-head`** — a flex row with a bottom rule, used by the reviewer to head a section; a candidate for a real section header in the questionnaire.
- **A working sticky pattern with the stacking order already thought through**: `.chrome` at z-index 30 top, `.sticky-footer` at 25 bottom, with the comment explaining why the header and banner were merged into one sticky block. A sticky section header would be a third tier and must clear 86px.
- **Animation precedent**: `@keyframes marking-pulse` on `.marking-banner.unmarked`, with a `prefers-reduced-motion` opt-out. It is the only keyframe animation in the file, and it establishes both the house pattern and the reduced-motion obligation for anything "sparkly".
- **`.card.tight`**, `.grid-2`, `.actions`, `.field`, `dl.kv`, `.table-wrap` — general layout helpers.
- **Localized repaint closures** inside `questionBlock` and `evidenceEditor`, as described in §6.
- `el()` accepts arbitrary attributes, `true` as a bare attribute, and `html` for raw markup, so `data-*`, `id`, `aria-*` and inline SVG are all available with no helper changes.

## 11. Her complaints mapped to the exact objects

- *"the evidence is a separate block, the questions is a separate block, but the whole thing just blends"* → `div.question` has a 1px `--line` top border and nothing else; the only tinted block is `.evidence`. Question, section card border, and page ground are all the same neutral.

She reads them as tabs; they render as a 43px flex row on a 4,415px card, and they scroll away.
- *"The overview, business, data, application, technology, these tabs … like in Excel, they would always be seen"* → `nav.stepper`, which is static and gone after 174px of a 20,190px page.
- *"a progress bar somewhere … that also needs to be always seen"* → the only always-visible progress today is `.footer-score .muted`, a muted grey sentence reading `"not scored yet - 0 of 176 answered"`. The `.step-bar` bars exist but scroll away with the stepper.
